name: Braised Chicken Cacciatore (Low-Carb Italian Chicken Stew)

fit.note: 495 cal is inside 400-650; 15g carb clears the 35g cap; batch-scales cleanly in a pot to 14. SEAFOOD FLAG: recipe uses 3 anchovy fillets dissolved as an umami base (Italian-braise/Caesar convention), NOT as a seafood main; I read the 'no seafood' condition as excluding seafood DINNERS, so this passes as a chicken braise, but the decider should confirm it wants trace anchovy in a low-carb run.

dupe_check.vs_catalog: NOT a duplicate of 'slow-cooker-chicken-cacciatore-pasta' (the only cacciatore in the 544-recipe digest): shares the cacciatore NAME and tomato-Italian sauce FAMILY, but only 2 of 4 axes match. Starch differs (this is a no-starch low-carb braise vs a penne-pasta dish), method differs (stovetop brown-then-simmer braise vs slow cooker), and the cut differs (bone-in thighs+drumsticks vs chicken breast). A pasta casserole and a low-carb braised stew are different dinners. No other tomato/red-wine braise in the accepted chicken set (fricassee=cream, marsala=marsala+mushroom no-tomato, tuscan=cream) collides.
dupe_check.vs_accepted_slugs: read fresh; no cacciatore or tomato-braise present.

cross_protein_collision_flag: Cacciatore-style braise (protein browned then simmered in tomato/red-wine/kalamata-olive/mushroom/capsicum sauce) is a portable 'hunter's stew' pattern. Watch for a same-structure twin in another protein's pool - a pork cacciatore, turkey cacciatore, or a rabbit/chicken-thigh 'hunter's braise' would be structurally the same dinner. Decider should run the cross-protein merge against any tomato-red-wine-olive braise.
evidence: Only cacciatore in catalog is the pasta-based slow-cooker version; this candidate is a distinct low-carb no-pasta stovetop braise, so it is a legitimate variation, not a near-duplicate.
